options: A confirmed, paying customer
A closed support ticket
A line item on a Quote
An unqualified prospect, not yet a customer
questions.explain: A Lead is an unqualified prospect, deliberately kept separate from Account, Contact, and Opportunity until it's converted.

questions.q: By default, what does converting a Lead create?
options: An Account, a Contact, and (optionally) an Opportunity
Only a new Case
A new Lead with a different owner
A Price Book entry
questions.explain: Lead conversion creates an Account and a Contact, and by default also creates an Opportunity unless that option is unchecked.

questions.q: What is the defining feature tracked on an Opportunity as it progresses?
options: Its Case Origin field
Its stage, shown as a path across the top of the record
Its Lead Source history
Its page layout assignment
questions.explain: An Opportunity moves through stages (Prospecting through Closed Won/Lost), displayed as a path at the top of the record.

questions.q: What does a Case typically represent?
options: A deal in the pipeline
A list of products for sale
A customer service issue or request
A marketing campaign
questions.explain: Case is the standard object for customer service issues and requests, usually tied to an Account and/or Contact.

questions.q: On a Case list view, what does "Change Owner" do?
options: Deletes the case permanently
Converts the case into an Opportunity
Reassigns the case to a different rep or queue
Marks the case as Closed - Converted
questions.explain: Change Owner reassigns a case to a different support rep or a queue, which is how case volume gets distributed across a team.
